headline: Neelsagar Express derails in Tangail, cutting rail links to north
summary: A coach of the Nil Sagar Express derailed at Mohera station, causing significant disruptions to trains traveling between Dhaka and the northern regions.
details: A coach of the Neelsagar Express derailed at Mohera railway station in Mirzapur, Tangail, around 9:00 AM on Thursday.
The derailment occurred as the train was passing through the station, causing four wheels of the guard's brake coach to go off the tracks.
No casualties or injuries were reported, though the incident caused panic among the approximately 1,000 passengers on board.
The train was eventually allowed to proceed toward Chilahati after leaving the derailed coach behind at around 11:00 AM.
The incident disrupted rail communication between Dhaka and the north, leaving several trains, including the Bonalata Express and Rajshahi Commuter, stranded at Tangail and Mirzapur stations.
According to station master Shahin Mia, the derailment was caused by wheel problems and also damaged a section of the track's point.
A relief train from Ishwardi is expected to arrive to remove the derailed coach and restore full service by 1:00 PM.
caption:
A Neelsagar Express coach derailed in Tangail, cutting off rail links to the north. No casualties reported.

A coach of the Neelsagar Express derailed at Mohera railway station in Mirzapur, Tangail, around 9:00 AM on Thursday.

The derailment occurred as the train was passing through the station, causing four wheels of the guard's brake coach to go off the tracks.

No casualties or injuries were reported, though the incident caused panic among the approximately 1,000 passengers on board.

The train was eventually allowed to proceed toward Chilahati after leaving the derailed coach behind at around 11:00 AM.

The incident disrupted rail communication between Dhaka and the north, leaving several trains, including the Bonalata Express and Rajshahi Commuter, stranded at Tangail and Mirzapur stations.

According to station master Shahin Mia, the derailment was caused by wheel problems and also damaged a section of the track's point.

A relief train from Ishwardi is expected to arrive to remove the derailed coach and restore full service by 1:00 PM.

headline_marked: [[Death penalty for Mahbub ul Alam Hanif]] in crimes against humanity case
headline: Death penalty for Mahbub ul Alam Hanif in crimes against humanity case
summary: The International Crimes Tribunal-2 has sentenced the joint general secretary of the banned Awami League to death, while three others received life imprisonment.
details: The International Crimes Tribunal-2 has sentenced Mahbub ul Alam Hanif, joint general secretary of the banned Awami League, to death in a crimes against humanity case.

Three other defendants—Sadar Uddin Khan, former chairman of Kushtia Zila Parishad, Asgar Ali, general secretary of Kushtia District Awami League, and Ataur Rahman, general secretary of Kushtia Municipal Awami League—were sentenced to life imprisonment.
The tribunal also ordered the confiscation of half of the properties of all four convicts.
The case involves three charges, including the killing of six people in Kushtia city. All four convicts, including Hanif, are currently fugitives.
The verdict was delivered on Thursday following the testimony of 18 witnesses and two rounds of arguments. Charges in the case were formally framed on November 2, 2025.
